notes:
Implemented as a MujocoDriver (DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: helper RosDriver replaced) over the card's first model, franka_description/mujoco/franka/dual_scene.xml, because the registry device plan is world.sim and the upstream world step/reset surface is the MJCF model; the ROS packages are ros2_control and gripper components without a world step/reset service. The fake is a package-local stand-in for the Python mujoco module, not a recording and not MuJoCo: it parses the MJCF and its includes for the joint dimensions, timestep and actuator ctrlranges and integrates placeholder first-order motion. It is declared F0 (the real-MuJoCo sim backend is F1 in fidelity_by_backend); no MuJoCo engine, ROS graph, simulator or hardware was contacted. The fake exposes and controls the 16 model channels that have a declared ctrlrange (14 torque motors and two gripper channels); the real dual scene has 44 channels, and the 28 position and velocity servo channels (which declare no ctrlrange) are outside the fake's control vector. The real sim backend would import mujoco and expose all 44; it was not run. cap.world.seed.v1 is not served because the MuJoCo bridge has no RNG seed control. The published action.ctrl limits are the SDK's derived model limits with ref dual_scene.xml:actuator_ctrlrange; the actual ctrlrange lines are cited in the facts at mj_dual.xml:452-506. Not covered: the upstream ros2_control controller layer and gain switching, the gripper action servers, rosbridge, cameras and rendering, real MuJoCo dynamics, and hardware. Left warnings: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (the fake is a simulator module stand-in with no Python native class) and G8.NO_UNIT x3 (ticks, seed and action.ctrl use model counts and model units, not physical units). driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null; no human [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation, all 19 facts, the fake and the derived envelope against mj_dual.xml, dual_scene.xml, objects.xml, the bringup launch and the MuJoCo hardware plugin at the pin. The fake hid the 28 position and velocity servo channels, which declare no ctrlrange (mj_dual.xml:452-506), and published a 16-channel control vector (seven torque motors and the gripper per arm, in another order) that the real engine, which compiles all 44 channels, does not have; a faithful 44-channel stand-in fails the gate because the SDK's MujocoBridge publishes unlimited channels as -/+1.7976931348623157e308 bounds that the envelope probe cannot exceed (the probe value is accepted and the integration turns non-finite: G6.ENVELOPE_NOT_ENFORCED for 56 bounds, G8 SAFE-014) and whose literals make the step tool 2,576 bytes (G8.TOOL_SIZE, limit 2,048), so no MJCF that mixes limited and unlimited actuators can pass at this SDK version. The docstring also said the repository exposes no world step/reset service, while the mujoco_ros server's set_pause, reset and Step action exist in the mujoco_ros_pkgs submodule, which the pinned parent tree records only as a gitlink, and the launch fact cited only line 149 for the MuJoCo-server include on 144-149. The reviewer made the fake report every actuator in document order (the servos not ctrl-limited, ctrlrange 0 0, as MuJoCo compiles them) and restore qpos0 (fake.py); rewrote the docstring, the actuator and launch facts and the gaps and added five facts (the libfranka real-robot interface that leaves safety to the controller, the submodule, the plugin's actuators-off initialisation, its gain switching and its per-mode ctrl writes) (driver.py); changed the cases to the 44-channel layout and qpos0 (test_driver.py); updated facts.md; and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails G6 and G8 exactly on that SDK defect (stable digest sha256:dca1504171444514a768008ad7703a8d1cae386395f3fbf96aac4c2a316acda5); the seven package cases pass, and collect.py reports RESULT_UNTRUSTED until the orchestrator writes status blocked. For the human reviewer: Blocked on the SDK, not on the model. Minimal repro: any MJCF with one motor that declares a ctrlrange and one position actuator that does not, served by MujocoDriver with a stand-in that reports both channels. Unblocking needs either a MujocoBridge representation for actuators without a ctrlrange (refuse them, take an operator envelope, or publish no bound and skip the probe) with a compact limit encoding, or a profile that mirrors the upstream plugin's gain switching (one actuator set per control mode, franka_mj_hardware_system.cpp:141-146, 508-547). The bare MJCF has all three actuator sets active at once with their XML gains, so even the real-engine backend is not the upstream runtime. The upstream's own world surface, the mujoco_ros server's ROS 2 API (set_pause with a success field, reset, a Step action), lives in the mujoco_ros_pkgs submodule, which the gate cannot read at the parent pin (the same gap as vision-agh/crazyflie-sim). The repository also drives real Franka Panda arms through FrankaMultiHardwareInterface and libfranka, whose documentation leaves all safety to the controller (franka_hardware.md:14): an arm path, R2 or higher if it is ever packaged; this package cannot reach it.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): SDK change MHS/changes/MUJOCO-UNBOUNDED-ACTUATORS.md removes the SDK_BUG this package was blocked on: the bridge now publishes one limit per control channel, the model's ctrlrange for the 14 torque motors and the two grippers and operator_required for the 28 position and velocity servos that declare none (mj_dual.xml:452-506), so a step that sets a servo is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET before the native step until an operator overlay bounds it; G6 exercises the 28 refusals, the conformance run probes all 44 channels, and the step tool is 1,727 bytes. The reviewer re-read the plugin's write path (franka_mj_hardware_system.cpp:259-299 refuses non-finite commands but clamps none), so no source states a servo bound and none is invented. Decision: fix, pass. Changed: site-limits.example.json (new: operator example data, a position servo bounded by its joint's range in mj_dual.xml, a velocity servo by the Panda joint velocity limit of panda_limits.h:14-16); driver.py (docstring without the blocked paragraph, the sim gap on the 28 servos, a fact citing panda_limits.h:14-16); facts.md (the Limits section and that fact); test_driver.py (the cases serve the example overlay with an in-range control vector, probe three servo bounds and check the LIMITS_UNSET refusal without an overlay); reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json regenerated. The gate passes G1-G9 with G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND and G8.NO_UNIT x3 (digest sha256:75cf5b61ca4c91e7f75897ab1c92b24dacc8bb34a8297efe553f35c62ae6472d). Still not covered and disclosed: the upstream plugin's gain switching (the bare model drives all three actuator sets at once), the mujoco_ros_pkgs submodule's world services, and the libfranka real-robot path. The card still names RosDriver: DECISION_DEVIATION stays until the orchestrator adds a mujoco routing override.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Different-model review of the reviewer edits made by claude-opus-5-5 with the SDK change MUJOCO-UNBOUNDED-ACTUATORS (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): The package was blocked SDK_BUG because 28 position/velocity servos have no ctrlrange; it now publishes 16 ranged channels as upstream_code and the 28 servos as per-element operator_required, and passes the gate (G6/G8 errors gone). The shipped site-limits.example.json is an example (reason starts 'example only:', issued_by operator:example), not a model bound. Evidence is contract_checked on the package's fake backend (MuJoCo itself was not run); this is a model review, not a human one.
